description.narrative:
Flexibelt svenskt stöd till ICJ strategiska plan 2026-2030 för ODA-fähiga aktiviteter under de första 3 åren 2026-2028.
Mål: 1. Främja utveckling, antagande och genomförande av internationella standards för mänskliga rättigheter 2. Stärka effektivitet och oberoende hos domare och advokater 3. Ökad tillgång till rättvisa och ansvarsutkrävande för alla
Aktiviteter: - Utveckling och främjande av standards och rättslig utveckling: Verka för normativ utveckling för mänskliga rättigheter och progressiv tolkning av existerande standards för att möta behov hos rättighetsbärare - Kapacitetsutveckling. Ge verktyg till domare, advokater och MR-försvarare i att applicera internationella standards effektivt - Påverkansarbete och rättshjälp: Samverka med stater, domstolar, internationella mekanismer för att påverka lag och policy som syftar till att ge ökat skydd för utsatta för MR-brott och ansvarsutkrävande - Partnerskap: Samverka med det globala nätverket av ICJs kommissionärer, nationella sektioner, CSOs för att säkra lokalt ägarskap för arbetet och större genomslag - Utveckla redskap och resurser för andra aktörer inom mänskliga rättigheter och rättsstatens principer: Handböcker för praktiserande, digitala verktyg för att göra komplexa ramverk begripliga, tillgängliga och möjliga att omsätta i praktik

Flexible Swedish support for the ICJ strategic plan 2026 - 2030 covering ODA eligible activities the first 3 years 2026-2028.
Goals: 1. Support and promote the development, adoption and implementation of international human rights law and standards 2. Strengthen the effectiveness and independence of judges and lawyers 3. Improve access to justice and accountability for all
Activities: - Standard-setting and legal development: Advocating for new human rights norms and progressive interpretation of existing standards to meet evolving needs
- Capacity strengthening: Equipping judges, lawyers, and human rights defenders with knowledge and tools to apply international law effectively. - Advocacy and legal assistance: Engaging with governments, courts, and international mechanisms to influence law and policy reforms and providing support to survivors to secure accountability. - Partnerships: Leveraging the global network of Commissioners, national sections, and civil society actors to amplify impact and ensure local ownership. - Developing tools and resources to support the work of others: Producing practitioner guides, legal principles, and digital resources to make complex norms accessible and actionable.

The ICJs theory of change is grounded in the principle that the rule of law and human rights are mutually reinforcing pillars of a just society. The organisation believes that systemic change occurs when legal frameworks are strengthened, legal professionals are empowered, and human rights defenders especially those most at risk are supported. By combining expert standard-setting, legal interventions, capacity-building, and advocacy at national and international levels, ICJ aims to create independent and accountable institutions that uphold justice.
The theory of change informs ICJs strategic goals and operational priorities. Planned actions include developing and defending international human rights standards, promoting their domestic implementation, and reinforcing judicial independence. ICJ will integrate emerging issues such as climate justice and digital rights into its legal strategies, ensuring that responses to new challenges remain rooted in human rights principles. The ICJ will pursue partnerships with civil society, bar associations, and judiciaries, while continuing evidence-based advocacy with multilateral, regional and national systems. These actions aim to close accountability gaps, protect civic space, and ensure that defenders can operate safely and effectively.
3 strategic goals will be pursued in the period 2026 - 2030
1. Support and promote the development, adoption and implementation of international human rights law and standards 2. Strengthen the effectiveness and independence of judges and lawyers 3. Improve access to justice and accountability for all
There are 3 expected outcomes:
1. International, regional and national institutions integrate and apply ICJ promoted human rights standards and legal principles i their decisions, policies and instruments, with demonstrable improvements in legal practice.
ICJ will track progress by measuring: # of ICJ recommendations adopted or cited in national / international legal instruments, court judgments, or UN resolutions, disaggregated by type and level of uptake (e.g., citation, endorsement, full adoption) # of instances ICJ publications are used as advocacy tools to support, defend and strengthen institutions, instruments and standards on rule of law and human rights # of recommendations or positions made to strengthen and defend national institutions, instruments, standards or resolutions on rule of law and human rights, and supported law and constitutional reform
2. Judges, lawyers and prosecutors demonstrate increased independence, professionalism, and capacity to uphold human rights and the rule of law, supported by ICJ interventions.
ICJ will track progress by measuring: % of participants in ICJ who report or demonstrate the application of international human rights standards in their decisions, pleadings, or legal opinions. Improved ability to conduct rights based legal analysis, with examples provided # of instances where ICJ interventions contributed to advancing judicial independence and protection of legal professionals, demonstrated through legal submissions, public advocacy, or documented changes in practice or awareness
3. Rights holders have better access to justice without discrimination, and state and non state actors are held accountable for their actions. ICJ will track progress by measuring: % of rights holders reporting improved ability to navigate justice systems after ICJ support, based on structured feedback. % of target group who report an enhanced understanding of subject matter following ICJ training # of individuals whose rights to a fair trial are increased through ICJ Trial. Monitoring # of litigation arguments submitted by the ICJ and partners/victims groups/HRDs with international, regional and national courts and bodies that are adopted
